summary: US-011: Festival skeleton — festival over shared-capacity day slots
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** to model a festival as a container of festival-day slots that draw on shared festival capacity, so TKT-14 can layer multi-day passes and zones onto a real structure.

**Priority:** P2
**Depends on:** US-009 (TKT-51 — festival-day is a slot kind), US-010 (TKT-52 — a festival groups like a season)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Catalog models a `festival` grouping festival-day slots (US-009 kind `festival_day`) that reference a **shared festival capacity** rather than per-day independent pools; the publication events express the shared-capacity relationship so inventory can provision it (TKT-14 consumes)
- [ ] API to create a festival, its days and the shared-capacity linkage; lifecycle (US-007) applies to the festival and cascades to its days; `organizer_id`-scoped throughout
- [ ] Public reads list a festival with its days as one grouped offer (ADR-004 TTL tier declared; browser-verified)
- [ ] **Non-goals (TKT-14):** multi-day pass products, zones/stages, RFID media, camping add-on — this story ships only the catalog skeleton + shared-capacity structure

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale; UI stories browser-verified with a screenshot in the PR; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002).

binding.rule: Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; lodging/day resources reserve through the same contention-safe core; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

APIs are contract-first: the OpenAPI spec is the source of truth, served by the service at /openapi.yaml and checked for drift in the gate; domain events use a versioned platform envelope (id, type==subject, occurred_at, schema, data) published to JetStream with acks (never fire-and-forget), with a deterministic envelope id so retried/raced emissions de-duplicate.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

reference.summary: PRD v1 — TKT-2 catalog & event structure user stories (US-007…US-011)
ADR-005 unified dated-slot admission — the load-bearing abstraction this epic hardens; §Consequences names re-entry/mid-day-capacity/weather-closure as the pressure tests
M1 catalog baseline: 0001_catalog_schema.sql (organizers/venues/events/performances/ticket_types), publish + performance.published event, aggregated TTL reads

comments.body:
Claimed TKT-53. Both blockers resolved: **TKT-51** (festival_day is a US-009 slot kind) and **TKT-52** (a festival groups like a season) are **Done** — open-blocker guard passes.

**Selection reason:** requested directly by the dev; it is the deepest node in the epic (TKT-2) dependency DAG and now unblocked, so it can proceed. Classification `complex` — full flow with the plan-approval gate (no `risk:low`).

Working in a dedicated worktree on branch `TKT-53-festival-skeleton` off `main` (parallel with another ticket). Drive style: **gates only**.

## Execution plan — TKT-53 (US-011 festival skeleton)

### Objective
Catalog ships a `festival` grouping `festival_day` slots that draw on **one shared festival capacity** (not per-day pools). Publish cascades festival→days and the publication event expresses the shared-capacity relationship so inventory can provision a single shared pool. `organizer_id`-scoped, public grouped read with an ADR-004 tier. **Out (TKT-14):** pass products, zones, RFID, camping, and the shared-capacity **claim mechanics** (ADR-005 amendment / ADR-010 keep capacity authority in inventory — catalog only emits the initial resolved shared capacity).

### Key modeling decisions (grounded in ADR-005 amendment + code map)
1. **`festivals` table = the capacity group.** A festival owns `shared_capacity int32` and is the target of the pre-installed `performances.capacity_group_id` seam (migration 0004 L37-39). So `capacity_group_id` FK-references `festivals(id)`. This makes "festival" and "capacity group" the same entity in v1 — the seam was named generically on purpose; we don't add a separate `capacity_groups` table (YAGNI until zones in TKT-14).
2. **Membership = festival_day slots only.** Attaching a slot to a festival requires `kind='festival_day'` (reject others with a typed error), same-organizer, draft-only membership (mirror `AttachPerformanceToSeries`'s frozen-after-launch gate). Sets `performances.capacity_group_id = festival.id`.
3. **Cascade like a series, not a season.** US-011 says lifecycle "cascades to its days". Reuse the `transitionSeries` precedent (lock festival + all member days `FOR UPDATE`, all-or-nothing preflight, per-member owed-emit markers). A festival spans days of potentially different events (season-like reach) but cascades publish/archive (series-like) — so it's a new grouping with series-style cascade over festival_day members.
4. **Shared capacity in the event = additive envelope extension (ADR-009-safe).** Add `capacity_group_id *uuid` + `shared_capacity *int32` to `PerformancePublishedData` (events.go L35-44), bumping catalog `Schema` from 2→3 (additive, inventory tolerates unknown/absent). When a festival_day publishes, its envelope carries the group id + the festival's shared capacity so inventory provisions ONE pool keyed by the group, not N per-slot pools. Also extend the internal read `/internal/performances/{id}` (server.go L120-123) with the same fields as the fallback path (inventory/consumer/catalog.go L29-54). **We do NOT change inventory's pool provisioning in this ticket** — that's TKT-14's claim mechanics; we only make the relationship *expressible* on the wire (AC #1 "so inventory CAN provision it").
5. **Public grouped read** `GET /public/festivals/{festivalId}` → festival name + its published festival_day slots as one offer, mirroring `GetPublicSeason` (server.go L754-770 / `GetPublishedSeason` store L958-996). TTL tier: **minutes** (`CacheControlPublicReads`, 300s) — same volatility class as event-detail/season reads per ADR-004 (a festival's day roster changes on the order of a publish, not seconds); rationale recorded in the OpenAPI path description.

### Test seam (TDD, red first)
Primary: `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go` with `fakeStore`/`fakePublisher` — copy `TestSeriesSeasonLifecycleAndPublicGrouping` (L1027). Add:
- `TestFestivalCreateAttachDaysAndSharedCapacity` — create festival w/ shared_capacity; attach two `festival_day` slots; reject a `performance`-kind attach (`ErrSlotKindMismatch`); reject cross-organizer; assert `capacity_group_id` set on days.
- `TestFestivalPublishCascadesToDaysAndEmitsSharedCapacity` — publish festival → both days flip published, two `performance.published` envelopes each carrying `capacity_group_id` + `shared_capacity`; idempotent re-publish emits nothing; archive cascade + owed-marker ordering (publication-before-archive).
- `TestFestivalPublicGroupedRead` — `GET /public/festivals/{id}` returns the two days as one offer; unpublished excluded; spec-validated by the gorillamux validator harness.
Store constraints (real PG, `//go:build smoke`): `migration_smoke_test.go` — new `festivals` table + FK from `capacity_group_id`, organizer scoping, and the draft-only membership CHECK. E2E: extend `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go` with a festival publish→JetStream(`Schema==3`, group id present)→`GET /public/festivals` path.

### Files to touch
- `services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0006_festivals.sql` (new) — `festivals(id, organizer_id FK, name jsonb, shared_capacity int, status, event/emit markers)`; add FK `performances.capacity_group_id → festivals(id)`; kind guard.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/store.go` — `Festival` type, `ErrSlotKindMismatch`, `FestivalTransition*` types.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go` — `CreateFestival`, `AttachDayToFestival` (lock+guards), `PublishFestival`/`ArchiveFestival` (reuse `transitionSeries` shape), `GetPublishedFestival`; write `capacity_group_id` in attach; select shared-capacity fields where days are read for publish.
- `services/catalog/internal/events/events.go` — extend `PerformancePublishedData` (+`capacity_group_id`,+`shared_capacity`), `Schema` 2→3, deterministic ids unchanged.
- `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` — `Festival*` schemas, `/festivals`, `/festivals/{id}/days`, `/festivals/{id}/publish`, `/festivals/{id}/archive`, `/public/festivals/{id}` (+ TTL note); then `make generate` (ripples model copies to inventory/commerce/payments/access — expected), keep drift gate green.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go` — handlers + `festivalToAPI`; extend `/internal/performances/{id}` payload; set `CacheControlPublicReads` on the public read.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/catalog.go` — accept the new fields on the internal read (tolerant; no provisioning change).

### Sequence
1. Red tests (server_test.go) → 2. migration 0006 + store types → 3. store methods → 4. events extension → 5. OpenAPI + `make generate` → 6. handlers + internal read → 7. green `make check` → 8. smoke/e2e + migration smoke → 9. storefront grouped listing + **browser-verify with screenshot** (AC #3) → 10. contract/OpenAPI drift green.

### Pre-mortem (how this fails)
- **Schema bump breaks inventory consumer:** mitigants — additive-only, absent fields tolerated; add an inventory consumer test asserting it still provisions on a schema-3 envelope with the new fields present *and* absent.
- **Scope creep into claim mechanics:** hard line — no pool-provisioning change in inventory; festival read/publish only. Assert in the PR body.
- **Cascade races (ADR / AGENTS.md row-lock rule):** festival publish/archive derives owed events from post-transition rows under concurrent archive/close — MUST use the locked-row decision pattern (`transitionSeries`/`ArchivePerformance`), decide under `FOR UPDATE`, emit at-least-once after commit. Do not conditional-UPDATE-then-reread.
- **`make generate` ripple:** the catalog spec change regenerates 4 other services' model copies + storefront api-types; commit them together or the drift gate fails.
- **Membership after launch:** festival_day attach must be draft-only (frozen post-publish) like series, else a late day dodges the cascade.

### Quality gates
`make check` green (lint+unit+integration, mirrors CI); contract test on touched boundaries (OpenAPI drift, ADR-009 envelope schema-3); `/public/festivals/{id}` ADR-004 tier declared (minutes) with rationale; storefront browser-verified + screenshot in PR; all entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002).

objective.note: Ship the festival catalog skeleton: a festival containing festival-day slots that draw on a shared festival capacity, so TKT-14 can layer multi-day passes/zones onto a real structure (epic COS #1, festival skeleton).

scope.note: IN: festival grouping festival_day slots (US-009 kind) referencing a shared festival capacity (not per-day independent pools); publication events expressing the shared-capacity relationship for inventory to provision; API to create festival + days + shared-capacity linkage; lifecycle (US-007) on the festival cascading to days; organizer_id-scoped; public reads listing a festival + its days as one grouped offer (ADR-004 tier). OUT (TKT-14): multi-day pass products, zones/stages, RFID media, camping add-on, and the actual shared-capacity claim mechanics (TKT-4).

uncertainties.note: The catalog/inventory boundary for shared festival capacity is decided by the US-008 spike + inherited by US-009's event shape; remaining choices (festival↔day↔shared-capacity modelling, cascade semantics) are engineering for Planning. No product decision pending here.

dependencies.note: Blocked-by TKT-51 (festival_day is a US-009 slot kind) and TKT-52 (a festival groups like a season). Both identified/linked; not claimable until both are Done (board open-blocker guard). It is the deepest node in the epic's dependency DAG.

approach.note: Add a festival grouping + shared-capacity reference in services/catalog over the US-009 typed slots and the US-010 grouping machinery; express the shared-capacity link in the publication envelope so inventory provisions it; cascade the US-007 lifecycle festival→days; new grouped public read with an ADR-004 tier. Contract-first.

first_slice.note: Vertical slice: create a festival with two festival_day slots on a shared capacity, publish → storefront lists them as one grouped offer (browser-verified), the shared-capacity relationship visible in the emitted event.

success.note: COS = the 4 ACs incl. the explicit TKT-14 non-goals + quality gates (make check, contract tests, ADR-004 tier, browser-verified).
